title: The agent-authority part of POST /authorise has no operation row, request shape or answer shape in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 062 Deviation screening agent in shadow E2b v1.md (sections 4, 10, 12, 17); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T-A.1, T-A.2, T6.1); _work/msr/context/P4.md (ownership rows and service row)
description: The legacy story needs an authority answer for one screening run: may this agent read, in which areas, and what is masked. The target has an authorise operation for role, scope and delegation of authority checks (Architecture v5 slide 14) and the P4 ownership rows list four other operations (GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants), but TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A carries no row for /authorise at all: it has API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is an authority check. No source names the agent-authority part of the request or of the answer, the caller type value, the trigger-event member, the capability-area and right members, the field-ID list, or the element that carries the two version labels. The same silence covers the event that would start the answer, and the only named authority shapes in the service are the /me/session session of API-P4-012 and the RBAC matrix of T6.1. The story fixes the part on the operation the service already publishes through RWB-P4-E1037-CON and holds the element names as the contract's, recorded as an assumption.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operation 'POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA)' and no shape; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no authorise operation; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives the letters only ('SY-AGENT Agent platform | R | R | -'); context pack P4 'REST operations provided (4)'; RWB-E1-062 section 12 names in-process interfaces (CaseQueryService.getCase, InteractionLedgerReader.list, DocumentQueryService.listByCase, RuleEvaluator.ownerFor) and no access call at all.
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 and the API specification owner
proposed: Confirm the agent-authority part and its element names at the wave 1 contract review with the P10 owner, add the authorise operation to the API specification index at its next revision, and keep the part inside the operation RWB-P4-E1037-CON publishes so no second authority path exists.

title: The reason-code vocabulary of a refusal and the status of each code are not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.4, AC-P4-004-01, AC-EXC-P4-004-01); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T6.2); RWB E1 062 (section 5 X7, section 14 MSG-P4-002)
description: The legacy story refuses a role without the right with 403 and MSG-P4-002 (section 5 X7, section 14) and the FSD repeats the shape for a screen (AC-EXC-P4-004-01, AC-ALT-P4-004-02), but no source gives a machine-readable reason for a refusal. A caller cannot tell a missing letter from a wrong role class from a scope that cannot be resolved, and the three cases carry different consequences for the caller and for the agent. The status mapping beyond 403 (422 for a malformed request, 503 for an entry that cannot be written) is inherited from the service's problem-response convention and is not written down for this operation either. The story fixes three reason codes and holds them as the contract's enumeration, recorded as an assumption, so a refusal stays legible without disclosing a case fact or a field value.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1 and VR-P4-004-2 ('An action outside the role's permission | MSG-P4-002') carry no reason; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-01 uses 404 with MSG-P4-003 for scope on a case read, so the scope refusal has two possible shapes; TSD P4 v3 T6.2 names the mechanism ('each endpoint declares its capability area and right; scope filters every query') and no code; RWB-E1-062 section 14 lists three message ids and no reason code.
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 and the security administrator role
proposed: Fix CALLER_KIND, RIGHT_NOT_HELD and SCOPE_NOT_ALL as the refusal reasons of the service's authorise operation, publish them in the API specification with their status, and confirm them once for every caller service so a cached guard answer reads the same code.

title: Which of the run's fields are personal for a non-human actor, and the mask format served to an agent, are not specified
source: RWB E1 062 (sections 4, 11, 17); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1 masking_rule, T7 NFR-039 and NFR-040); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.5, AC-ALT-P4-004-01, AC-EXC-P4-004-05)
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 AC5; 8 BR5; 11 Data; 13
description: The masking answer is defined per role and per field ID, and the FSD fixes the shapes a screen shows: XXXXXXXXX1234 for an identity number, XXXXXX5678 for a phone number and XXXX-XX-XX for a date (AC-ALT-P4-004-01, AC-EXC-P4-004-05). Nothing states what the same fields look like when the caller is an agent, and nothing lists which of the agent's four reads carry a personal value at all: the legacy names the ledger summary (DF-INT-011) and the stored document field value (DF-DOC-015) as 'Read (masked)' in its data table (section 11) and no other field. Whether a document field the agent reads with a confidence is masked whole or by field id, and whether the party identifiers of the case read are presented to the agent at all, are therefore decisions and not values. The story answers one marker per presented field ID with the default-deny rule and the two legacy fields masked, and records the field list and the format as an assumption until the masking owner fixes them.
evidence: RWB-E1-062 section 11 marks DF-INT-011 and DF-DOC-015 'Read (masked)' and marks no other field; section 17 says 'call note summaries are masked before the model call'; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule carries role_code, field_id and unmasked and no format; TSD P4 v3 T7 NFR-039 says 'masked ... on every screen and every agent call, by role' with no format; FSD P4 v3 A2.5 fixes the three shapes for a screen only.
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer and the security administrator role
proposed: Fix the personal field list of the four agent reads and the mask format served to a non-human caller with the masking owner, load it as a masking version rather than as code, and prove it with a synthetic value that must appear in no answer, no log and no span.

title: The default scope of the agent service identity is not specified for this legacy key
source: RWB E1 062 (sections 4, 10); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1 role.default_scope, T3.2 LOV-SCOPE, T6.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.14)
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 AC1; 8 BR4; 10 Authority
description: A role carries one default scope from LOV-SCOPE: OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL. The agent reads cases of every team and region in the shadow sample of 200 cases, which only ALL permits, but no source states the scope of a non-human actor role, and no table of rwb_access binds a role to a list of teams or regions, so a narrower scope could not be resolved even if it were set. The story answers ALL with no restriction and refuses a narrower scope with SCOPE_NOT_ALL instead of resolving a list that does not exist, and records the value as an assumption so the matrix owner sets it explicitly rather than leaving it empty.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role.default_scope is REQUIRED with list LOV-SCOPE; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE = OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 gives SY-AGENT letters per area and no scope; FSD P4 v3 A2.14 scopes a user 'by team and region' and names no non-human rule; RWB-E1-062 section 10 gives the agent reads across the sample and no scope value.
proposed: Set the service identity of the agent platform to scope ALL in the matrix version in force and state the rule for every non-human actor role in the access and administration documentation, so the choice is data and not a default of the reader.

title: The access entry of an agent read has no source row, element list or decision-code vocabulary of its own
source: RWB E1 062 (section 10); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.7, AC-P4-007-01, AC-ALT-P4-007-02, AC-EXC-P4-007-04); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T6.2, T7 NFR-042)
description: The FSD fixes the access entry of a screen read: decision code AC-READ, the actor, the case ID, the time and the field IDs returned with their masked marker (AC-P4-007-01), the export entry AC-EXPT with the filter and the row count (AC-ALT-P4-007-02) and the refusal entry AC-DENY with its reason (AC-EXC-P4-007-04). It says nothing of a read by a service identity: no source says whether the entry carries the agent code, the policy version, the autonomy mode or the trigger event, whether a non-human read is an AC-READ at all, and which of the run's identifiers are recorded. The service also has no access-log table of its own, so the entry is the append of the access and decision chain written by RWB-P4-E1039-APP, whose columns are the library's. The story records the members it needs for an auditable agent read and holds them as an assumption.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-007-01 lists 'decision code "AC-READ", actor "U-4101", the case ID and decided at 10:15' and 'the field IDs returned, with DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked "masked"'; AC-EXC-P4-007-04 lists AC-DENY, the area and the right; TSD P4 v3 T6.2 and T7 NFR-042 say 'every read ... is logged' with no entry shape; RWB-E1-062 section 10 lists the roles and their rights and no entry content.
owner_role: Internal audit role and the solution architect, P4
proposed: Fix the entry members of a non-human read in the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP and publish them once for every service identity, so an audit query by agent code and policy version answers from the same chain as the screen entries.
